pages.lesson:
LESSON: LISTENING FOR GIST: ATTENTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.6: Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what is your father’s name?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify members of the family
2. respond to oral questions from a text on naming members of the nuclear family
3. appreciate the roles of immediate family members

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING FOR GIST: ATTENTIVE LISTENING
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING FOR GIST: ATTENTIVE LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify members of the family

What this means
In this part you learn to identify members of the family. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify members of the family.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify members of the family. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to oral questions from a text on naming members of the nuclear family

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to oral questions from a text on naming members of the nuclear family. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to oral questions from a text on naming members of the nuclear family.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to oral questions from a text on naming members of the nuclear family. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the roles of immediate family members

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the roles of immediate family members. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the roles of immediate family members.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the roles of immediate family members. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify members of the family)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening to a partner. (skill: respond to oral questions from a text on naming members of the nuclear family)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the roles of immediate family members)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify members of the family.
3. Practise this skill: respond to oral questions from a text on naming members of the nuclear family.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the roles of immediate family members.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what is your father’s name?
2. Why should we pronounce words correctly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify members of the family.
5. Be able to: respond to oral questions from a text on naming members of the nuclear family.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
